answer: A sybil farmer's profit is cheap fakery: shells claiming work nobody re-checks. Hold every claim to the lantern of randomized replication — a randomly drawn peer re-derives a sample using the published recipe. Real work is timber: solid under re-examination, and replicators earn for confirming it. Fakes snap: a mismatch convicts the shell, wipes its standing, and paints a violet flag on its operator's other identities for priority audit. The farmer must either do the work for real on every shell — no longer cheap — or fake claims and gamble against audits it can't predict.
